dimensions.assessment: Affects recreational boaters, fishers, divers, and state/local entities, as well as federal agencies and tribal organizations.
dimensions.evidence: consult with relevant stakeholders (including state and local governments, Indian tribes, and Native Hawaiian organizations)

dimensions.assessment: Primarily administrative and informational, providing public access to geographic information system data without altering underlying laws or regulations.
dimensions.evidence: directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to standardize and publish geospatial data

dimensions.assessment: The source does not specify explicit federal spending amounts or major revenue impacts, focusing instead on data coordination and publication.
Requires new data standardization, interagency coordination, and a publicly accessible website managed by NOAA.
dimensions.evidence: develop and adopt standards with respect to the coordination and dissemination of geospatial data

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent ongoing requirements for updating data twice a year or in real time, beginning within a multi-year implementation window.
dimensions.evidence: update-- (1) the data described in subsections (a)(1) and (b) not less frequently than 2 times each year

missing_information: Exact dollar amounts for federal appropriations or implementation costs are not stated in the source.
importance_detail.rationale: This act requires NOAA to standardize and publish geospatial data related to public recreational use of federal waterways on a public website, coordinating with various stakeholders and federal agencies over a multi-year period.
